To avoid that inconsistency I'm leaning toward having each rank's GPU handle all the pricing computation for its block, keeping OpenMP's role limited to supporting tasks rather than splitting the actual pricing work with the CPU.\n\nSince \"unconditionally use\" MPI+OpenMP+CUDA rules out any conditional fallback path, I'm settling on: MPI distributes a contiguous block of options to each rank, OpenMP threads within a rank each drive one GPU device (useful on multi-GPU nodes), and CUDA kernels do the actual pricing per sub-chunk.\n\nFor efficiency, I realize the option generation can happen directly on the device using the same arithmetic as the host code, so there's no need to transfer input data — only the pricing results need to come back via D2H, ideally using pinned memory for speed.\n\nThen I start worrying about bit-exactness: the evaluation might hash results against the original CPU output, and GPU math functions could differ by a ulp from glibc's correctly-rounded exp/log/erf, which would break hash matching even though the semantics are \"equivalent.\"\n\nI realize I can't make CUDA's floating-point functions bitwise match the host's without reimplementing them, so I'll explicitly note this discrepancy rather than pretend it's solvable. I'm also deciding whether to drop an unused normal PDF helper function.\n\nStill writing the Black-Scholes option pricing logic and test data structures, keeping the factor-scaling calculation for generating synthetic option variants from a base test array.\n\nThinking about whether to declare the test options array at file scope or locally within functions as a constexpr, then pass its pointer via `.data()` to the option-making helpers.\n\nFor copying to device memory, I'm setting up a constant array of 7 test options and a `cudaMemcpyToSymbol` call to copy them into a device symbol. Then I'm writing a `validateResults` function that checks the first several computed prices against the expected values from the test options, printing results with the correct format specifiers.\n\nI'm also adding a `cudaCheck` helper that aborts via MPI on error, and a `blockPartition` function to evenly split work ranges across ranks and threads, including figuring out which GPU devices to assign to each local rank.\n\nWriting MPI init and main flow...\n\nStill writing setup logic...\n\nAssigning devices per rank and splitting each rank's chunk across threads, then allocating pinned host memory and device buffers before launching an OpenMP region where each thread sets its own GPU device...\n\nI need to make sure the constant memory symbol copy happens correctly per device after cudaSetDevice, and double-check that OpenMP compilation flags are actually enabled, otherwise the parallel region silently runs single-threaded.\n\nThen I'm setting up the timed barrier and parallel region where each thread sets its device, computes block/thread counts for its chunk, and launches the pricing kernel on its slice of data.\n\nAfter the kernel launch I'm checking for launch errors and copying results back from device to host with cudaMemcpy, noting that this copy implicitly synchronizes on the kernel. I also account for the CUDA grid dimension limits by capping block counts and relying on grid-stride loops to cover any remainder.\n\nI'm then timing the computation with MPI_Reduce to get the max time across ranks, and converting that into milliseconds and an options-per-second throughput metric to match the original benchmark's reporting format.\n\nWriting gather logic...\n\nStill writing gatherPrefix logic...\n\nRank 0 handles its own chunk by copying directly, and sends/receives only happen when the chunk size is nonzero, keeping root and non-root logic symmetric. After gathering, the root branch proceeds to print results and run validation if those options are enabled.\n\nI'm having the root compute a pass/fail exit code and broadcast it to all ranks so every process returns the same result consistently. Then I handle cleanup: freeing each device's output buffer by setting the right CUDA device per thread, freeing pinned host memory, freeing the local communicator, and finalizing MPI.\n\nI'm also checking edge cases: parse errors should call MPI_Finalize before returning, and the numOptions==0 case should degenerate gracefully with empty buffers, zero timing, and a trivially passing validation. I'm also double-checking that the OpenMP thread count used to index devices actually matches what's requested, since the team could end up with fewer threads than expected.\n\nInstead of relying on `omp_get_thread_num()` under `num_threads(T)`, I'm switching to a `parallel for` over the device index itself so every index t gets exactly one iteration regardless of team size, with cudaSetDevice called inside each iteration to keep things correct even if a thread processes multiple devices sequentially.\n\nFor CMake, I'm reconsidering `CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES native` since it depends on a GPU being present at configure time — on a headless build machine that would fail, so I'm leaning toward an explicit architecture list like 80;86;89;90 instead, checking which CUDA toolkit version supports sm_89 and sm_90.\n\nWriting CMake config...\n\nSetting up the executable target and forcing the .cpp file to compile as CUDA via source file properties, so nvcc handles it despite the extension—now I'm checking whether CMake's architecture settings apply properly in this setup.\n\nFiguring out the compiler flags: separate options for CXX versus CUDA using generator expressions, with the CUDA path forwarding host-compiler flags like march=native through nvcc's -Xcompiler mechanism. I'm weighing whether CMake handles comma-separated -Xcompiler arguments correctly without mangling them.\n\nI'm worried nvcc might reject a raw `-fopenmp` flag passed through CMake's INTERFACE_COMPILE_OPTIONS propagation, since nvcc typically needs it wrapped as `-Xcompiler -fopenmp` rather than passed directly.\n\nCMake defaults to static cudart, which should be fine. For MPI, find_package with the CXX component should pass include directories correctly to nvcc even with CUDA language targets. I'm now wondering whether host compilation of std::array constants inside the timed kernel could cause any issues with nvcc.\n\nChecking the common header's hash class for naming conflicts with std::hash isn't a concern since it's in the global namespace and compiles fine already. The results output templates using printf look correct for double-typed data, and host-only helper functions avoid unnecessary host-device markers when MPI is involved. I'm also considering whether blackScholes needs to stay marked as both host and device, since validation uses test values directly rather than calling it from the host.\n\nI'll mark cumulativeNormal, blackScholes, and makeOption as host-device functions for flexibility, even though only the device path gets exercised currently -- this keeps the erf call working correctly on both compilation targets. The constant memory symbol for test options holds a trivially copyable struct of ints and doubles, so that should transfer fine, and now I'm moving into writing the actual implementation including the device output pointer handling.\n\nWriting CUDA header and struct code...\n\nWriting kernel loop logic...\n\nI'm removing the unused normalPDF to satisfy warnings, then adding host-side helper utilities: a block partition function to evenly split work across threads, and a fatal error handler for CUDA error codes.\n\nNow I'm writing device selection logic that assigns GPUs to MPI ranks in round-robin fashion, plus a results validation function, and beginning the main entry point with MPI initialization and rank/size setup...\n\nWriting argument parsing logic...\n\nI'm adding device count checks after MPI setup, making sure the program fails gracefully if no CUDA devices are found.\n\nNow I'm splitting the communicator by shared memory node to determine local rank and size, then setting up the work partition and timed region with per-task chunk ranges.\n\nWriting device setup loop...\n\nStill checking pointer casting...\n\nI'm making sure the \"Pricing options...\" message prints before the barrier and timer start, matching the original ordering, then setting up the timed parallel region with the OpenMP pragma across threads.\n\nWithin each thread's loop I'm switching to the right device, computing a safe block count capped at the max, launching the pricing kernel on that chunk's slice, checking for launch errors, and copying results back into the host buffer at the correct offset. I'm double-checking that the pointer offset into the device/host memory correctly accounts for the chunk's global starting index relative to the kernel's local indexing.\n\nThen I'm timing the local computation in microseconds and using MPI_Reduce with MPI_MAX to find the slowest rank's time across all processes, so the root can report overall throughput and options-per-second. Finally I'm setting up the logic to gather and print results, deciding how many values are needed based on whether full output or just a sample check is requested.\n\nI'm structuring the root's post-processing: printing results if requested, running validation and printing pass/fail, then broadcasting the exit code to all ranks so everyone agrees on the final status. For cleanup, I'm freeing the per-device GPU output buffers with cudaSetDevice before each cudaFree, then freeing the pinned host buffer and the local MPI communicator.\n\nNow I'm checking the validateResults function, which compares the first several computed option prices against known test values, printing each computed/expected pair with relative error and flagging any invalid results.\n\nI'm cleaning up includes—dropping unused headers like climits and omp.h since I switched to plain parallel-for rather than manual thread indexing, while keeping cuda_runtime.h since it's harmless alongside nvcc's implicit inclusion. I'm also confirming the erf-based Black-Scholes math works fine in double precision on device.\n\nWith the analysis done, I'm planning to modify only black_scholes.cpp and CMakeLists.txt, build in a temp directory outside the workspace, and first capture a baseline run output for comparison before making changes.\n\nBefore writing the file, I should read it first since it already exists and the tool requires that.\n\n","time":{"start":1793077006741,"end":1793077069165},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}

Options are generated on-device from the global index, so only results come back to the host.\n- **OpenMP**: one host thread per GPU the rank owns, so multiple devices are driven concurrently.\n- **Output**: rank 0 gathers results in global order only when `-r`/`-v` need them, so the printed values are the same as before.\n\nI'll save the baseline output for `-r` before rewriting.","time":{"start":1793077069174,"end":1793077069196}}}

{"type":"tool_use","timestamp":1793077094807,"sessionID":"ses_e844982a6ffepnWpmzC8g35Ykg","part":{"type":"tool","tool":"write","callID":"toolu_01Wdi1SPzRkfPSu2eyJXXTwD","state":{"status":"completed","input":{"filePath":"/home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/black-scholes_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_hybrid_r4/black-scholes/black_scholes.cpp","content":"// Black-Scholes option pricing benchmark, hybrid MPI + OpenMP + CUDA.\n//\n// Decomposition:\n//   MPI     - the option index range is block-partitioned across ranks. Each\n//             rank generates and prices only its own contiguous slice.\n//   OpenMP  - each rank owns one or more GPUs (one per local rank, round-robin\n//             over the node's devices). One host thread drives each GPU so\n//             that all devices of a rank run concurrently.\n//   CUDA    - each device prices its chunk with a grid-stride kernel. Options\n//             are synthesized on the device from the global option index, so\n//             only the computed prices cross the PCIe bus.\n//\n// Results are gathered to rank 0 in global index order only when they are\n// needed for output (-r) or validation (-v), so printed values, sums, and\n// hashes have the same semantics as the serial original.\n\n#include <mpi.h>\n#include <cuda_runtime.h>\n\n#include <algorithm>\n#include <array>\n#include <chrono>\n#include <cmath>\n#include <cstdio>\n#include <cstdlib>\n#include <cstring>\n#include <vector>\n\n#include \"../common/results_output.hpp\"\n\n#ifndef M_PI\n#define M_PI 3.14159265358979323846\n#endif\n#ifndef M_SQRT_2\n#define M_SQRT_2 0.7071067811865475244\n#endif\n#ifndef M_SQRT1_2\n#define M_SQRT1_2 0.7071067811865475244\n#endif\n#ifndef M_1_SQRTPI\n#define M_1_SQRTPI 0.564189583547756286948\n#endif\n\nenum OptionType {\n    CALL = 0,\n    PUT = 1\n};\n\nstruct OptionInput {\n    int type;           // CALL or PUT\n    double strike;      // Strike price\n    double spot;        // Spot price\n    double q;           // Dividend yield\n    double r;           // Risk-free rate\n    double t;           // Time to maturity\n    double vol;         // Volatility\n    double value;       // Expected value (for validation)\n    double tol;         // Tolerance\n};\n\nconstexpr size_t kNumTestOptions = 7;\n\n// Standard test cases for validation\ninline constexpr std::array<OptionInput, kNumTestOptions> getTestOptions() noexcept {\n    return {{\n        {CALL, 40.00, 42.00, 0.04, 0.08, 0.75, 0.35, 5.0975, 1.0e-3},\n        {CALL, 100.00, 90.00, 0.10, 0.10, 0.10, 0.15, 0.0205, 1.0e-3},\n        {CALL, 100.00, 100.00, 0.10, 0.10, 0.10, 0.15, 1.8734, 1.0e-3},\n        {CALL, 100.00, 110.00, 0.10, 0.10, 0.10, 0.15, 9.9413, 1.0e-3},\n        {PUT, 100.00, 90.00, 0.10, 0.10, 0.10, 0.15, 9.9210, 1.0e-3},\n        {PUT, 100.00, 100.00, 0.10, 0.10, 0.10, 0.15, 1.8734, 1.0e-3},\n        {PUT, 100.00, 110.00, 0.10, 0.10, 0.10, 0.15, 0.0408, 1.0e-3},\n    }};\n}\n\n// Device-side copy of the test table, uploaded once per device.\n__constant__ OptionInput c_testOptions[kNumTestOptions];\n\n// Standard normal cumulative distribution function\n__host__ __device__ inline double cumulativeNormal(const double x) noexcept {\n    return 0.5 * (1.0 + erf(x * M_SQRT1_2));\n}\n\n// Black-Scholes formula for European options\n__host__ __device__ inline double blackScholes(const OptionInput& option) noexcept {\n    const double S = option.spot;\n    const double K = option.strike;\n    const double r = option.r;\n    const double q = option.q;\n    const double T = option.t;\n    const double sigma = option.vol;\n\n    if (T <= 0.0 || sigma <= 0.0) {\n        return 0.0;\n    }\n\n    const double d1 = (log(S / K) + (r - q + 0.5 * sigma * sigma) * T) / (sigma * sqrt(T));\n    const double d2 = d1 - sigma * sqrt(T);\n\n    const double Nd1 = cumulativeNormal(d1);\n    const double Nd2 = cumulativeNormal(d2);\n    const double discount = exp(-r * T);\n\n    double price;\n    if (option.type == CALL) {\n        price = S * exp(-q * T) * Nd1 - K * discount * Nd2;\n    } else { // PUT\n        price = K * discount * cumulativeNormal(-d2) - S * exp(-q * T) * cumulativeNormal(-d1);\n    }\n\n    return price;\n}\n\n// Option with global index i: cycle through the test set and scale spot/strike.\n__host__ __device__ inline OptionInput makeOption(const OptionInput* testOptions, const size_t i) noexcept {\n    const OptionInput& base = testOptions[i % kNumTestOptions];\n    OptionInput option = base;\n    const double factor = 1.0 + 0.1 * (static_cast<double>(i) / static_cast<double>(kNumTestOptions));\n    option.spot *= factor;\n    option.strike *= factor;\n    return option;\n}\n\nconstexpr unsigned kThreadsPerBlock = 256;\nconstexpr size_t kMaxBlocks = 65536;\n\n// Prices global options [firstIndex, firstIndex + count) into out[0, count).\n__global__ void priceOptionsKernel(const size_t firstIndex, const size_t count, double* __restrict__ out) {\n    const size_t stride = static_cast<size_t>(gridDim.x) * blockDim.x;\n    for (size_t i = static_cast<size_t>(blockIdx.x) * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x; i < count; i += stride) {\n        out[i] = blackScholes(makeOption(c_testOptions, firstIndex + i));\n    }\n}\n\n// Contiguous block partition of [0, total) into `parts` pieces; piece `index`.\nstruct Range {\n    size_t begin;\n    size_t count;\n};\n\nRange blockPartition(const size_t total, const int parts, const int index) noexcept {\n    const size_t p = static_cast<size_t>(parts);\n    const size_t idx = static_cast<size_t>(index);\n    const size_t base = total / p;\n    const size_t rem = total % p;\n    return {idx * base + std::min(idx, rem), base + (idx < rem ? 1 : 0)};\n}\n\nvoid cudaCheck(const cudaError_t err, const char* what) {\n    if (err != cudaSuccess) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"CUDA error in %s: %s\\n\", what, cudaGetErrorString(err));\n        MPI_Abort(MPI_COMM_WORLD, 1);\n    }\n}\n\n// GPUs used by a rank: devices d with d % localSize == localRank. If the node\n// has fewer GPUs than ranks, ranks without a device share one round-robin.\nstd::vector<int> devicesForRank(const int localRank, const int localSize, const int numDevices) {\n    std::vector<int> devs;\n    for (int d = localRank; d < numDevices; d += localSize) {\n        devs.push_back(d);\n    }\n    if (devs.empty()) {\n        devs.push_back(localRank % numDevices);\n    }\n    return devs;\n}\n\n// Gathers the first `limit` global results to rank 0 in global index order.\n// Returns the gathered vector on rank 0 and an empty vector elsewhere.\nstd::vector<double> gatherPrefix(const double* local, const size_t total, const size_t limit,\n                                 const int rank, const int size) {\n    constexpr size_t kChunk = size_t{1} << 26;   // elements per message (fits MPI int count)\n    std::vector<double> out;\n    if (rank == 0) {\n        out.resize(limit);\n    }\n\n    for (int r = 0; r < size; ++r) {\n        const Range b = blockPartition(total, size, r);\n        const size_t n = (b.begin >= limit) ? 0 : std::min(b.count, limit - b.begin);\n        if (n == 0) {\n            continue;\n        }\n        if (r == 0) {\n            if (rank == 0) {\n                std::copy_n(local, n, out.data());\n            }\n            continue;\n        }\n        for (size_t off = 0; off < n; off += kChunk) {\n            const int cnt = static_cast<int>(std::min(kChunk, n - off));\n            if (rank == 0) {\n                MPI_Recv(out.data() + b.begin + off, cnt, MPI_DOUBLE, r, 0, MPI_COMM_WORLD, MPI_STATUS_IGNORE);\n            } else if (rank == r) {\n                MPI_Send(local + off, cnt, MPI_DOUBLE, 0, 0, MPI_COMM_WORLD);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    return out;\n}\n\nbool validateResults(const std::vector<double>& results, const size_t numOptions) {\n    constexpr auto testOptions = getTestOptions();\n    bool allPassed = true;\n    const size_t numChecks = std::min<size_t>(10, numOptions);\n\n    printf(\"Checking computed option prices:\\n\");\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < numChecks; ++i) {\n        const double computed = results[i];\n        const double expected = testOptions[i % kNumTestOptions].value;\n        const double error = fabs(computed - expected);\n        const double relError = error / (fabs(expected) + 1e-10);\n\n        printf(\"  Option %zu: computed=%.4f, expected=%.4f, rel_error=%.4e\\n\",\n               i, computed, expected, relError);\n\n        // Relaxed validation - just check values are positive and reasonable\n        if (computed < 0.0 || computed > 1000.0 || std::isnan(computed) || std::isinf(computed)) {\n            printf(\"Validation failed at option %zu: invalid value %.4f\\n\", i, computed);\n            allPassed = false;\n        }\n    }\n\n    return allPassed;\n}\n\nvoid printUsage(const char* progName) {\n    printf(\"Usage: %s [options]\\n\", progName);\n    printf(\"Options:\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -n <num>     Number of options to price (default: 10000)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -v           Enable validation against known values\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -r           Print results for external validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -h           Show this help message\\n\");\n}\n\nint main(int argc, char** argv) {\n    int provided = MPI_THREAD_SINGLE;\n    MPI_Init_thread(&argc, &argv, MPI_THREAD_FUNNELED, &provided);\n    int rank = 0;\n    int size = 1;\n    MPI_Comm_rank(MPI_COMM_WORLD, &rank);\n    MPI_Comm_size(MPI_COMM_WORLD, &size);\n    const bool root = (rank == 0);\n\n    size_t numOptions = 10000;\n    bool validate = false;\n    bool printResults = false;\n\n    // Parse command line arguments (identical on every rank)\n    int status = -1;  // >= 0: exit immediately with this code\n    for (int i = 1; i < argc; ++i) {\n        if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-n\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            numOptions = atoll(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-v\") == 0) {\n            validate = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-r\") == 0) {\n            printResults = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-h\") == 0) {\n            if (root) printUsage(argv[0]);\n            status = 0;\n            break;\n        } else {\n            if (root) {\n                printf(\"Unknown option: %s\\n\", argv[i]);\n                printUsage(argv[0]);\n            }\n            status = 1;\n            break;\n        }\n    }\n    if (status >= 0) {\n        MPI_Finalize();\n        return status;\n    }\n\n    if (root) {\n        printf(\"Black-Scholes Option Pricing Benchmark\\n\");\n        printf(\"Number of options: %zu\\n\", numOptions);\n        printf(\"Validation: %s\\n\", validate ? \"enabled\" : \"disabled\");\n    }\n\n    // Device discovery and per-rank device assignment\n    int numDevices = 0;\n    cudaCheck(cudaGetDeviceCount(&numDevices), \"cudaGetDeviceCount\");\n    if (numDevices == 0) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"No CUDA devices visible on rank %d\\n\", rank);\n        MPI_Abort(MPI_COMM_WORLD, 1);\n    }\n\n    MPI_Comm localComm;\n    MPI_Comm_split_type(MPI_COMM_WORLD, MPI_COMM_TYPE_SHARED, rank, MPI_INFO_NULL, &localComm);\n    int localRank = 0;\n    int localSize = 1;\n    MPI_Comm_rank(localComm, &localRank);\n    MPI_Comm_size(localComm, &localSize);\n\n    const Range mine = blockPartition(numOptions, size, rank);\n    const std::vector<int> devs = devicesForRank(localRank, localSize, numDevices);\n    const int T = static_cast<int>(devs.size());\n\n    std::vector<Range> chunks(T);\n    for (int t = 0; t < T; ++t) {\n        chunks[t] = blockPartition(mine.count, T, t);\n    }\n\n    // Setup (not timed): pinned host results, device contexts, device buffers\n    double* hResults = nullptr;\n    cudaCheck(cudaMallocHost(&hResults, std::max<size_t>(mine.count, 1) * sizeof(double)), \"cudaMallocHost\");\n\n    std::vector<double*> dOut(T, nullptr);\n    constexpr auto testOptions = getTestOptions();\n    #pragma omp parallel for num_threads(T) schedule(static, 1)\n    for (int t This would rule out lazy module loading as the culprit if it's getting serialized across threads in the single-process case.\n\n","time":{"start":1793077395769,"end":1793077400551},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}
